issue_context.title: Cleanup/Enhance scheduler metrics
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->
I'd like to propose the following changes to `pkg/scheduler/metrics/metrics.go`. 

For metrics to be deprecated, should do it in **two phases** in order to maintain some sort of backwards compatibility. This is not mandatory as all scheduler metrics are ALPHA now.
1. Mark the metrics as deprecated in 1.18
2. Remove metrics in 1.19

### Remove metrics marked as deprecated
Currently handled in #76496 

### Change `framework_extension_point_duration_seconds` from sampling to always record
We were concerned by performance so we sample framework/plugin metrics. We should continue sampling plugin metrics since there are so many plugins and some plugins run per node. However, we can probably alway record extension point metrics. We should run the benchmark and make sure the overhead is negligible. 

### Deprecate `predicate/priority` related metrics
* `scheduling_algorithm_predicate_evaluation_seconds`, replaced by `framework_extension_point_duration_seconds[extenstion_point="Filter"]`
* `scheduling_algorithm_priority_evaluation_seconds`, replaced by `framework_extension_point_duration_seconds[extenstion_point="Score"]`

### Deprecate `scheduling_duration_seconds` Summary metric
We already have Histogram metrics recording the same info. 
Prefer Histogram over Summary because: 
* Histogram is aggregatable
* Histogram supports ad-hoc quantile computation while Summary requires predefined quantiles
* Some monitoring systems such as Stackdriver don't have a Summary equivalent

Although Summary metric is less expensive on the server side, its limitations make it less desirable. See https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/ for detailed comparison.

This metrics is currently used by clusterloader2 tests, see [code](https://github.com/kubernetes/perf-tests/blob/44971cd21c3a33916402bc13b4ec049d097e9263/clusterloader2/pkg/measurement/common/scheduler_latency.go#L124-L133). We have to update the test to use corresponding Histogram metrics.




/sig scheduling
cc @ahg-g @Huang-Wei
